headline: IBM says it will give chip designers an early design kit for its 0.7-nanometre Nanostack chip technology in the first quarter of 2027.
score_reason: Lowered from 5 to 4: IBM announced this on 13 Oct, three days before this edition, and the pool headline overstated an early research kit.
importance_line: It matters to chip designers, design-software vendors and equipment makers preparing for a new transistor layout, and to AI chip makers short of on-chip memory space, but it is an early research kit for a technology that is not ready for wide use.
summary: IBM Research said on 13 Oct 2026, as Wccftech reported on 16 Oct, that it plans to make an early research design kit available in the first quarter of 2027 for its 0.7-nanometre (7-angstrom) Nanostack manufacturing technology, which stacks the two kinds of transistors on top of each other instead of side by side, so that chip firms, design-software vendors and equipment makers can explore it. IBM says the technology offers nearly double the transistor density of its 2-nanometre chip and 40 percent better scaling of SRAM, the on-chip memory that has barely shrunk in recent chip generations, but the first kit will not hold every model of a mature commercial kit.
notes: Pool source Wccftech read; the original IBM Research post (13 Oct 2026 per Google News) read and used as source. Wccftech says the technology launched in June; IBM says 'earlier this year'. Event older than the window; the editor decides whether it prints.
